method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: sheet 12 (north) prints '27TH ST.' with neighbour '14' and '80'' rotated in the corridor; north-side evens read '302 304 306 308 310 312', '314 316 318 320 322 324' (Ave C-D), '402 404 406 408 410 412', '414 416 418 420 422 424' (Ave D-E), then '502 504' east of Ave E; Ave F frontage closes 2624/2626/2628. sheet 14 (south) prints '27TH ST.' at its top margin with neighbour '12'; south-side odds read '301 303 305 307 309 311', '313 315 317 319 321 323', '401 403 405 407 409 411', '413 415 417 419 421 423', then '501 503' - the exact odd complement of sheet 12's evens, with the 300/400/500 change at Ave D and Ave E. Evens on the north side and odds on the south side interlock one-for-one and the hundred-block changes fall on the avenues named in each key map, so the read line is the shared corridor and not the block-pitch (~1160-1180 px) neighbour street.
note: Reported value is the drafted corridor CENTRELINE in that sheet's own working-raster pixels (work/sheets/1912w/u<N>.jpg, the same pixels the green rulers label), following the pair_33_34 convention. sheet 12 north face sheet-wide mean 3624.9 + 120 px half-width; sheet 14 both faces read sheet-wide (mean N 77.5 / S 319.5, drafted width 242). full C-F overlap; sheet-wide means used. The drafted 80' corridor measures 239-245 px on these plates; centreline sigma ~3 px, plus ~2 px where a half-width had to be supplied. Each plate's frontage tilts 8-13 px across the sheet, so the reading window was matched to the two plates' shared avenue. Detection's candidates were all block-interior or siding lines (e.g. sheet 11 cand1 y=3558 falls inside the Pattern & Casting warehouse, 200 px north of the corridor centre) and none were used.
